studios.title: Project Explanation Studio
studios.description: Explain a project clearly, distinguish your own contribution, discuss technical decisions, and describe evidence and limitations.

questions.prompt: Choose one project. What problem does it address, who is it for, and what does it do?

followup.prompt: What is one concrete user journey that shows the problem and how your project addresses it?

prompts.guided: What problem were you trying to solve? Who experiences it, and what does your project help them do?
prompts.standard: What is one concrete user journey that shows the problem and how your project addresses it?
prompts.challenging: What evidence supports the problem being worth solving, and what alternative solution did you reject?

questions.prompt: What did you personally design, build, or verify? Be clear about your own work versus the team's work.

followup.prompt: Pick one part you personally implemented. What did you change, and how can someone verify it?

prompts.guided: Which part did you personally work on? What did you do first, and what changed?
prompts.standard: Pick one part you personally implemented. What did you change, and how can someone verify it?
prompts.challenging: What was the hardest engineering decision in your contribution, and how would you defend it in a code review?

questions.prompt: Describe one important technical decision. What alternatives or constraints did you consider?

followup.prompt: If the main constraint changed, what would you reconsider and why?

prompts.guided: What options did you have, and what made you choose this one?
prompts.standard: If the main constraint changed, what would you reconsider and why?
prompts.challenging: What failure mode or scale limit could invalidate this choice, and how would you test that?

questions.prompt: How did you test the project, what evidence do you have, and what remains incomplete?

followup.prompt: Tell me about one failure or limitation you found. How did you investigate it, and what would you do next?

prompts.guided: What did you test, what happened, and what is still not checked?
prompts.standard: Tell me about one failure or limitation you found. How did you investigate it, and what would you do next?
prompts.challenging: Which result is strongest evidence that it works, what does that evidence not prove, and what experiment comes next?

studios.title: HR & Behavioural Interview Studio
studios.description: Practise structured, truthful examples about teamwork, conflict, setbacks, learning, motivation, and professional judgement.

questions.prompt: Tell me about yourself and the kind of role or opportunity you are preparing for.

followup.prompt: Which experience or project best supports that introduction, and what was your specific contribution?

prompts.guided: What is one experience that shows the kind of work you enjoy?
prompts.standard: Which experience or project best supports that introduction, and what was your specific contribution?
prompts.challenging: What differentiates your experience from another candidate's, and what evidence can you point to?

questions.prompt: Describe a time you worked with other people toward a shared goal. What was your role?

followup.prompt: How did you coordinate when people had different priorities or working styles?

prompts.guided: What was the shared goal, and what part did you take responsibility for?
prompts.standard: How did you coordinate when people had different priorities or working styles?
prompts.challenging: Describe a disagreement that changed the plan. How did you reach a decision and what was the outcome?

questions.prompt: Tell me about a difficult problem, mistake, or setback. What did you do?

followup.prompt: What would the people involved say you handled well, and what would you change next time?

prompts.guided: What happened, what did you do, and what did you learn?
prompts.standard: What would the people involved say you handled well, and what would you change next time?
prompts.challenging: What assumption failed, how did you respond under pressure, and what process change prevents recurrence?

questions.prompt: Why are you interested in this role, and what would you want to learn in your first few months?

followup.prompt: What have you done so far to understand the role or build the skills it needs?

prompts.guided: What interests you about this role, and what would you like to learn?
prompts.standard: What have you done so far to understand the role or build the skills it needs?
prompts.challenging: Which part of the role will be most challenging for you initially, and what is your concrete plan to close that gap?

studios.title: Technical Interview Studio
studios.description: Explain core CS concepts in your own words, use examples, reason about trade-offs, and acknowledge uncertainty accurately.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between an array and a linked list. When might you choose each?

followup.prompt: What is the cost of accessing an element by index in each structure, and why?

prompts.guided: Can you give a small example of each structure and how you would use it?
prompts.standard: What is the cost of accessing an element by index in each structure, and why?
prompts.challenging: How do insertion patterns and memory locality affect the choice between these structures?

questions.prompt: Walk me through what happens when a browser sends an HTTP request to an API and receives a response.

followup.prompt: Where would you investigate first if the request returns a 500 response, and what evidence would you inspect?

prompts.guided: Can you describe the request and response using a simple example?
prompts.standard: Where would you investigate first if the request returns a 500 response, and what evidence would you inspect?
prompts.challenging: How would you distinguish a client error, server error, network failure, and timeout in an investigation?

questions.prompt: What is a database index? Explain the benefit and one trade-off of adding an index.

followup.prompt: Why might an index fail to improve a particular query, or even make writes slower?

prompts.guided: Can you explain what the index stores and why that helps a lookup?
prompts.standard: Why might an index fail to improve a particular query, or even make writes slower?
prompts.challenging: How would you use a query plan to decide whether an index is useful, and what would you measure?

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a process and a thread? Give a practical example.

followup.prompt: What kinds of problems can occur when threads share mutable data, and how can a program reduce that risk?

prompts.guided: Can you give an example of work that belongs to a process and work that belongs to a thread?
prompts.standard: What kinds of problems can occur when threads share mutable data, and how can a program reduce that risk?
prompts.challenging: Compare a lock and message passing for coordinating concurrent work. What trade-offs would guide your choice?
